role.altitude: The upholsterer keeps measuring, choosing materials, drawing patterns, matching fabric and talking with customers; working out yardage by hand, laying out cutting plans piece by piece, copying job cards into a spreadsheet and calculating quotes on paper shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping the model material table current
role.ambitious_version: An upholsterer whose records and quotes build themselves from the bench, leaving the hands for the craft.

tasks.short: Read work orders, inspect and measure the piece, decide material types, and determine amounts of materials required to cover workpieces.

steps.what: Upholsterer inspects and measures the workpiece
Upholsterer applies knowledge of materials to decide the types of fabric, foam and webbing
Upholsterer works out the amounts of materials required

tasks.design: For standard furniture models, the shop system holds a material table per model (fabric length per width, foam, webbing), and the upholsterer adjusts for pattern repeat instead of calculating from scratch. Reading the order, measuring and choosing material types stay with the upholsterer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Yardage was worked out by hand for each job.
tasks.enabler_now: Material tables per model in the shop system.
tasks.still_hard: Antique and custom pieces with no model.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing how much a fabric stretches over a curved arm.

reach.learn: Whether orders match need more closely.

evidence.claim: Furniture production software processes orders automatically from standard models.

assumptions: Boundary: determining materials; cutting plans (task 14247) and customer estimates (task 14238) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s4: material tables per standard model, covering about 50% of jobs; s4 is priced at that share.
Reading, measuring and deciding keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of jobs on standard models.
research_questions: Does fabric waste per job fall?

incremental.description: Upholsterer updates the material table after new models.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: material tables cover only a quarter of jobs because most pieces are antique or custom (3.4); high: tables cover about 50% of jobs as assumed (8.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Interpret sketches, customer descriptions or blueprints, draw upholstery cover patterns, lay out the cutting plans, and check pattern matching before cutting.

steps.what: Upholsterer interprets the sketch, customer description or blueprint and measures
Upholsterer draws the upholstery cover patterns
Upholsterer lays out the pieces on the fabric to make the cutting plans
Upholsterer checks pattern matching and the plan before cutting

tasks.design: For pieces with digital patterns, nesting software lays out the cutting plan with fixed rules for grain line, fabric width, stripe and pattern matching, instead of the upholsterer laying out pieces one by one. Interpreting the design, drawing new patterns and checking matching by eye stay with the upholsterer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cutting plans were laid out by hand on the table.
tasks.still_hard: Large repeats and odd fabrics that need matching by eye.
tasks.human_edge: Centring a motif on a seat back.

evidence.claim: Furniture production software generates markers and spread plans.
An upholstery maker reported around 9% material savings after moving to such software; vendor case, no baseline given, no time figures.

assumptions: Boundary: patterns and cutting plans; determining material amounts (task 14233) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s3: digital patterns exist for about 60% of jobs; s3 is priced at that share.
Interpreting, drawing and checking keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of jobs with digital patterns.
research_questions: Does layout time per job fall without matching errors?

incremental.description: Upholsterer sets nesting rules for new fabrics.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: digital patterns exist for only about a quarter of jobs and large repeats are matched by eye (5.5); high: about 60% of jobs with digital patterns as assumed (13.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record start and stop times per job, copy job card times into the shop spreadsheet and total them, and note reasons for delays or rework, to maintain records of time required for each job.

steps.what: Upholsterer records start and stop times per job: on the job card today, by tapping start and stop on the bench tablet after the change
Upholsterer copies job card times into the shop spreadsheet and totals them per job
Upholsterer notes the reason for delays or rework

tasks.design: A tablet at the bench lists open work orders; the upholsterer taps start and stop on the job instead of writing times on a card, and the records app totals time per job, so the job cards are no longer copied into the shop spreadsheet. The upholsterer still adds the reason for a delay or rework. Times are used per job for costing and quotes; using them to judge individual upholsterers needs works council consent first.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper job cards were copied into a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Simple records apps on a bench tablet.
tasks.still_hard: Jobs interrupted many times a day.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why an old frame took twice as long.
tasks.altitude: Much less copying; the work stays.

reach.learn: Whether labour norms per model become more accurate.

evidence.claim: Logs tied to an operator can measure performance, so the works council must consent.
A simple records app replaces the paper job card; a person adds only the reason for a stop.

assumptions: Boundary: job time records; cost estimates (task 14238) use the records.
s2 saves the second entry of job cards into the spreadsheet.
Tapping start and stop is the upholsterer's own record and takes about as long as writing the time on a card, so s1 keeps its full time.
Works council consent is obtained before times are linked to people.
unknowns: Number of job changes per day.
research_questions: Are job costs known sooner after completion?

incremental.description: Upholsterer corrects missed taps at day end.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: jobs interrupted many times a day are kept on cards, so about half of the cards are still copied (14.5); high: all jobs on the tablet (29.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss upholstery fabrics, colors and styles with customers, measure the piece, calculate the cost estimate, write the quote, check it, and give it to the customer.

steps.what: Upholsterer discusses upholstery fabrics, colors and styles with the customer, showing samples
Upholsterer measures and inspects the furniture for the estimate
Upholsterer calculates the cost estimates: fabric, materials and labour
Upholsterer checks the final quote: fabric, amounts, labour hours and price against the customer's choice and the piece
Upholsterer gives the quote to the customer

approvals.approved_version: The quote with fabric, materials, labour and price exactly as checked by the upholsterer in s5, given once to the customer named in it for the piece named in it; any change needs a new check before it is given.

tasks.design: An estimate calculator takes the model or measurements, the chosen fabric and its price from the supplier price list, and labour hours from the shop's norms per model, and prints the quote, instead of the upholsterer calculating on paper and typing a letter. Discussing fabrics and styles and measuring stay with the upholsterer, who checks and gives that quote.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quotes were calculated on paper and typed.
tasks.enabler_now: Estimate calculators with price lists and labour norms.
tasks.still_hard: Antique pieces where hidden frame damage changes the price.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a customer choose a fabric they will still like in ten years.

evidence.claim: Estimate calculators price materials from price lists and labour from norms.

assumptions: Boundary: discussing and estimating; determining job materials (task 14233) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s3: supplier price lists loaded by the shop office and labour norms derived from the job time records of task 14237, covering about 60% of quotes; s3 is priced at that share.
Discussing, measuring, checking and giving the quote keep their full time.
research_questions: Do quotes match final job costs more closely?

incremental.description: Upholsterer reviews labour norms each quarter.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most quotes are for antique pieces outside the labour norms, so they are still worked out and written by hand (7.7); high: about 60% of quotes covered as assumed (15.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
